title: Protocol for Pig Vagus Nerve Microdissection and Histology
author: Megan Settell
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.9ieh4be
materials: a. Sigma Aldrich, Pure Ethyl Alcohol, Product #: 459844

steps.title: Expose Vagus Nerve
steps.instruction: Expose the right or left side vagus nerve from the pharyngeal branch to the recurrent laryngeal bifurcation using careful dissection to avoid disturbing any branches.

steps.title: Document Nerve Trajectories and Anatomy
steps.instruction: Capture images of the trajectories of the superior laryngeal (SL), recurrent laryngeal (RL), and vagus nerves.

substeps.instruction: Note the presence, arrangement, and lengths of the internal superior laryngeal (ISL) and external superior laryngeal (ESL) from bifurcation to muscle insertion.
Measure diameters of ISL and ESL approximately 1mm from the nodose ganglion.

steps.title: Perform Standard Subject Measurements
steps.instruction: Obtain the following standard measurements from each subject:

substeps.instruction: SL to carotid bifurcation (measured from the valley at the top of the bifurcation)
SL to the mandible (bend in the jaw)
SL to sternal notch
Distance from SL to the most cranial LIFE electrode
Distance from SL to the most caudal LIFE electrode

steps.title: Measure LivaNova Cuff Distances
steps.instruction: Determine the distance from the LivaNova epineural stimulating cuff to the RL and SL branches:

substeps.instruction: Proximal contact of LivaNova cuff to SL
Distal contact of LivaNova cuff to SL
Proximal contact of LivaNova cuff to RL
Distal contact of LivaNova cuff to RL

steps.title: Measure SL and RL Dimensions
steps.instruction: Measure the length and diameter of the SL and RL nerves:

substeps.instruction: Length of SL from nodose to bifurcation into external/internal branches
Length of SL to insertion in muscle
Diameter of SL 1mm from the nodose ganglion
Length of RL from bifurcation to insertion into muscle
Diameter of the RL at the bifurcation
Distance from SL to recurrent bifurcation

steps.title: Measure Vagus Nerve Diameter
steps.instruction: Obtain vagus nerve diameter measurements at the following locations:

substeps.instruction: 1cm caudal to SL
6cm caudal to SL
At the RL bifurcation

steps.title: Map Nerve Terminations and Associated Branches
steps.instruction: Identify where each of the recurrent and superior laryngeal branches terminate and identify any associated branches.

steps.title: Calculate Distance to RL Branch Termination
steps.instruction: Determine the distance from the stimulating electrode to the RL branch termination in the cricoarytenoid using the following values:

substeps.instruction: Distance from RL into termination (from step 6c)
Distance from SL to RL bifurcation (from step 6e)
Distance from SL to stimulating LivaNova cuff (from steps 5a and 5b)

steps.title: Determine Electrode to RL Insertion Distance
steps.instruction: Determine the distance from the location of the stimulating electrode to the recurrent laryngeal insertion as it runs back up near the electrode along the esophagus.

steps.title: Locate Additional Nerves
steps.instruction: Determine the location and trajectory of the aortic depressor nerve (if found), the sympathetic chain (running parallel or bundled), the pharyngeal branch, and any other associated branches.

substeps.instruction: Distance from RL bifurcation to experimental transection cut locations and to the insertion in the muscle
Distance from RL bifurcation to the location of LIFE electrodes in the vagus trunk

steps.title: Prepare Nerve Samples for Histology
steps.instruction: Prepare and process the nerve samples for histological analysis:

substeps.instruction: Apply histological dye (Bradley Products, Inc., Davidson Marking System, Bloomington, MN) to the lateral and ventral edges to maintain orientation.
Place samples in neutral buffered formalin for ~24 hours at 4°C.
Process samples in a histology tissue processor for 13 hours (including standard dehydration with ethanol 50-100%, clearing with xylene, and paraffin infiltration).
Embed samples in paraffin wax and allow to set for approximately 24 hours.

steps.title: Section and Mount Samples
steps.instruction: Cut and mount the paraffin-embedded samples:

substeps.instruction: Remove excess wax until samples are visible.
Place samples in an ice water bath for approximately 1 hour.
Cut 5 um sections using a Leica Biosystems Rotary Microtome (Buffalo Grove, Illinois).
Float samples in a 35-40°C water bath and mount on a glass slide.
Allow slides to dry overnight.

steps.title: Perform Gomori’s Trichrome Staining
steps.instruction: Stain the slides in a fume hood, consulting SDS sheets for all chemicals:

substeps.instruction: Place slides in xylene (Sigma Aldrich, Product #: X54) for 3 minutes (2x).
Place slides in 100% Ethanol (Sigma Aldrich, Pure Ethyl Alcohol, Product #: 459844) for 2 minutes (2x).
Place slides in 95% Ethanol (prepared from pure Ethyl Alcohol) for 2 minutes (2x).
Place slides in 70% Ethanol (prepared from pure Ethyl Alcohol) for 2 minutes.
Rinse slides in deionized water for 1 minute.
Place slides in Bouin’s Solution (Sigma Aldrich, Product #: HT10132) in a 60°C water bath for 1 hour.
Rinse slides in running cold tap water until clear.
Place slides in Weigert’s Iron Hematoxylin (Sigma Aldrich, Product #: HT1079) for 10 minutes.
Place slides under running cold tap water for 5 minutes.
Place slides in Gomori’s Trichrome Stain (Sigma Aldrich, Product #: HT10516) for 20 minutes.
Place slides in 1% Glacial Acetic Acid solution (Sigma Aldrich, Product #: 695092) for 1 minute.
Place slides in 95% Ethanol for 1 minute.
Place slides in 100% Ethanol for 1 minute (2x).
Place slides in xylene for 1 minute (2x).
Apply a drop of mountant xylene substitute (ThermoFisher Scientific, Product #: 1900231) and coverslip.
Allow slides to dry for approximately one hour.

steps.title: Scan and Export Images
steps.instruction: Collect images of the stained slides using a Motic Slide Scanner (Motic North America, Richmond, British Columbia):

substeps.instruction: Conduct a preview scan of the entire slide.
Select areas of interest and scan at 20x using the EasyScan scanning application (Motic China Group Co., LTD).
Export images to tiff format using the Motic VM conversion application (Version 3.0, Motic China Group Co., LTD).
